content: 1. The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a significant role in the metabolism of chlordiazepoxide. Rifabutin and rifampin can decrease the levels of chlordiazepoxide by enhancing its metabolism through this pathway. These interactions are considered minor, but their clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Clidinium can potentiate the effects of rimabotulinum toxin B through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction may lead to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 3. Chlordiazepoxide and risperidone both increase sedation when used together. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Therapy modification, such as lowering the benzodiazepine dose, is recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 5. Rolapitant increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This effect can persist for at least 28 days after administration. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Rucaparib increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Chlordiazepoxide and sage both increase sedation. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 8. Chlordiazepoxide increases sedation, while salmeterol decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Chlordiazepoxide and skullcap both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 10. The combination of chlordiazepoxide and sodium oxybate can result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 11. Stiripentol can increase or decrease the effects of chlordiazepoxide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, as it acts as both an inhibitor and inducer of this enzyme. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Chlordiazepoxide and sufentanil both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. The combination of sufentanil and chlordiazepoxide can lead to hypotension, profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death. Avoid or use alternative drugs if possible. 13. Suvorexant and chlordiazepoxide both increase sedation. Dosage adjustments of suvorexant and other CNS depressants may be necessary. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Chlordiazepoxide and tapentadol both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Tazemetostat decreases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Tecovirimat decreases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 17. Teduglutide increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by enhancing the absorption of concomitant oral medications. Caution is advised with drugs requiring titration or those with a narrow therapeutic index. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 18. Chlordiazepoxide and temazepam both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Terbinafine increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Assess the need to reduce the dose of CYP2D6-metabolized drugs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Chlordiazepoxide increases sedation, while terbutaline decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Chlordiazepoxide and thioridazine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 22. Chlordiazepoxide and thiothixene both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification, such as lowering the benzodiazepine dose, is recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 24. Chlordiazepoxide and topiramate both increase sedation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Chlordiazepoxide and tramadol both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Chlordiazepoxide and trazodone both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 27. Chlordiazepoxide and triazolam both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Chlordiazepoxide and triclofos both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Chlordiazepoxide and trifluoperazine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Chlordiazepoxide and trimipramine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Triprolidine and chlordiazepoxide both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Tucatinib increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling. 33. Valerian and chlordiazepoxide both increase sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Chlordiazepoxide increases the effects of vinpocetine through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction may enhance memory improvement, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 35. Voriconazole increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 36. Chlordiazepoxide increases sedation, while xylometazoline decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Chlordiazepoxide increases sedation, while yohimbine decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Chlordiazepoxide and ziconotide both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 39. Chlordiazepoxide and ziprasidone both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 40. Zolpidem and chlordiazepoxide increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to additive CNS depression. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 41. Chlordiazepoxide and zotepine both increase sedation. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Chlordiazepoxide and zuranolone increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 43. Chlordiazepoxide, a benzodiazepine, depresses all levels of the central nervous system (CNS), including the limbic system and reticular formation, possibly by enhancing gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) activity, a major inhibitory neurotransmitter. 44. Clidinium, an anticholinergic agent, exerts antispasmodic and antisecretory effects on the gastrointestinal tract. 45. Chlordiazepoxide has a half-life of 6–24 hours and is metabolized in the liver to active metabolites, including demoxepam, desmethylchlordiazepoxide, desmethyldiazepam, and oxazepam. It is excreted in the urine.
